1099: 9. What was learned by running it (2026-10-21 to 23, fed back into the design)
1100: Stages 01–07 were implemented in ftphase and run through for Al–Li (ACE, examples 5, 6 and 8), Ni–Al (Mishin 2009 EAM, example 7) and Ag–Cu (example 9, in progress). The equations and the division into stages did not need to change, but the following points are added as design notes. The source of the numbers is the respective section of ftphase.html.
1104: For fcc Al–Li, the difference between a 64-atom icet SQS and the average of two 32-atom random configurations is −3 to +1 meV/atom at 800 K. Configuration noise does not move the eutectic temperature but moves the solubility limit by 0.01–0.05.
1105: For solid solutions, use the average of several configurations and the half-width as the error. The SQS is icet's fixed-supercell MC (5 s).
1106: The sqsgenerator 0.5.6 wrapper called a non-existent API (sqs_optimize) and did not work (ported to parse_config → optimize, 2026-10-23). Comparing random / icet SQS / sqsgenerator for fcc Al–Li (examples/alli_sqs_compare.py, ACE): sqsgenerator takes 0.1–0.3 s for 5 × 10⁵ iterations (icet's fixed-supercell MC 4–6 s); the first-shell Al–Li Warren–Cowley parameter is |α| ≤ 0.07 for all three. The icet cluster-vector residual (pairs + triplets) at 64 atoms is 0.02–0.11 for icet, 0.11–0.31 for sqsgenerator and 0.21–0.51 for random. The differences in 0 K energy and 800 K QHA G at 64 atoms relative to icet are +0.1 to +1.2 meV/atom for sqsgenerator and −1.3 to +0.7 meV/atom for random (up to −3.7 meV/atom at 32 atoms).
1107: With 64 atoms or more, the difference between generators is about 1 meV/atom, within the 2 meV/atom configuration noise. The default is icet (optimised up to triplets, smallest residual). sqsgenerator is fine when many compositions must be generated quickly.
1108: The fixed phonopy mesh [4,4,4] has only 64 q-points for cells with a small primitive cell, and F of fcc Al was 8.8 meV/atom too high at 900 K (Al melting point 850 → 890 K). Near the melting point the QHA is 20–45 meV/atom above calphy's solid-phase TI (Ni, anharmonic).
1109: The mesh is specified by density (60 Å). Solid phases above about 0.8 T_m are replaced by calphy's solid-phase TI (Frenkel–Ladd + reversible scaling) (the route of Eqs. (D1)(D2) is for the low-temperature side). The upper limit of the TI sweep is taken above the temperature at which the phase disappears (in Ni–Al an artefact appeared where phases vanished at the cap).
1110: calphy's liquid-phase TI on the GPU (KOKKOS; hybrid/scaled/kk from LAMMPS 30 Sep 2026 onwards) is 1.7–3.3 times faster than 4 CPU ranks. The reproducibility spread between seeds is 1.3–1.4 meV/atom (ACE Al–Li); the run-to-run scatter after averaging is 0.1–0.5 meV/atom.
1111: Average 2–3 runs per composition and use the scatter as the Monte Carlo σ (lower bound 1.4 meV/atom).
1112: Fitting a polynomial to a G that contains k_B T x ln x cannot reproduce the end-point slopes and produces spurious miscibility gaps. Splines through defect cells create a spurious B2+B2 two-phase region from sampling noise.
1113: Ideal mixing (Eq. (E1)) and the sublattice entropy (Eqs. (E9)–(E13)) are separated analytically and the fit is applied only to the excess term (liquid: ideal mixing + Redlich–Kister). The defect energies of ordered phases are fitted linearly per branch on either side of the stoichiometric composition.
1114: Mixing quantum QHA solids with classical TI liquids lowers the ACE Al melting point by 40 K; the harmonic correction F_q − F_cl recovers 10 K (the rest is the difference between QHA and TI).
1115: Bring all phases to the same level (classical) before taking the convex hull.
1116: Unless the grid is restricted to temperatures where liquid runs exist at all compositions, the hull sees a truncated liquid and creates spurious intervals. A "two-phase region" of the same phase is fit curvature if its position does not move under Monte Carlo.
1117: The grid is determined by the liquid coverage. Same-phase intervals are shown as fit noise on the grounds of zero standard deviation. Boundaries at the edge of the sampled range get an edge flag.
1119: Both the Slurm dependency chain (examples 5–7) and the AiiDA WorkChain (examples 8 and 9, ftphase.txdiagram) ran to completion independently of a session. In AiiDA the daemon exported PYTHONPATH and broke conda inside the jobs (removed by the compute host's prepend).
1120: Heavy stages (03A/03B) are CalcJobs, light stages (01/02/04–07) are calcfunctions. Resubmission runs only the unfinished parts.
1122: Al–Li (ACE, classical): eutectic 760–770 K at x ≈ 0.31 (experiment 875 K, 0.24, Okamoto 2012); temperatures are uniformly 40–120 K low. Ni–Al (EAM): B2 congruent melting 1861 K (experiment 1911; two-phase MD with the same EAM 1850 ± 25); the Ni-side width of B2 appears but the Al-side vacancy width does not.
1123: The temperature offsets are a problem of the potential and the classical level, not of the stages. The Al-side width of the ordered phase requires a sublattice model including thermal defect pairs (Wagner–Schottky).
